key_insight: Probe geometry strongly controls material flow and gap-bridging in wire-based friction stir welding, enabling sound joints across large gaps when the pin design is optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that W-FSW can join high-strength EN AW-2024 T351 Alclad with much higher gap tolerance while retaining strong mechanical performance, making it promising for industrial repair and assembly.
method: Tested 10 stirring probe geometries in wire-based FSW.
Used continuous wire feeding to bridge a 4 mm joint gap.
Assessed weld quality via X-ray, metallography, hardness, and tensile performance.
evidence_signal: The best probe design (P6) achieved about 85% transverse and 89% longitudinal base-material strength, with refined grains down to ~2.55 μm and predominantly sound welds in successful cases.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on probe design and process window, so gap bridging may not generalize without careful parameter optimization and quality inspection.
paper_title: Effect of stirring probe geometry on gap-bridging mechanisms and joint strength in wire-based friction stir welding of EN AW-2024 T351 Alclad
